clauses.trace: The only rollback test fails pkg-b's CHANGELOG.md write (it is a directory, EISDIR) after pkg-a's package.json and CHANGELOG were already written. It asserts exact bytes of pkg-a package.json, pkg-a CHANGELOG (binary bytes), the untouched changeset and pkg-b package.json. In applyReleasePlanUnjournaled the changeset deletion/rename (index.ts ~L190-L232), the pre.json removal in exit mode (L114-L120) and the creation of .changeset/pre (L187) all happen after that failure point, so none of them is exercised. Restoring a deleted changeset, restoring a deleted pre.json, undoing a renamed changeset and removing the created pre directory are untested.
Asserts err.cause is an Error with code EISDIR, so the cause is the original error.

boundaries.boundary: failure after package.json and changelog writes of an earlier package
failure after changesets were deleted (or renamed into .changeset/pre) and pre.json removed
directory .changeset/pre created by the run is removed on rollback

gap.missing: No test makes the failure happen after the destructive steps (changeset deletion, rename into .changeset/pre, pre.json removal, creation of .changeset/pre). Rollback of deleted files and of created directories is therefore unproved.
gap.reproduction: Case 1: set a pre-release preState (mode 'pre') with a changeset, with no .changeset/pre dir, and make one changeset operation fail after the others succeed (for example mock fs.rename to reject for the second changeset). Assert the rejection's cause is the injected error, .changeset/pre does not exist, every changeset is back at its original path with its exact bytes, and no dot-journal remains. Case 2: preState mode 'exit' with .changeset/pre.json present, fail after pre.json is removed (for example a failing formatter or a failing changeset rm); assert pre.json bytes are restored. Case 3: fail on the second changeset delete and assert the first, already deleted, changeset is restored.

clauses.trace: A writeFile spy snapshots .changeset the first time a package.json is written. It asserts exactly one dot-prefixed entry exists at that moment, so the journal is recorded inside .changeset with a leading dot before the first change. The code fsyncs the journal.
After a successful run and after a rolled-back run, no dot-prefixed file remains in .changeset.
The journal format is left to the implementation (JSON with base64 entries); no assertion is needed.

boundaries.boundary: journal exists before the first file change
journal removed after success and after rollback

clauses.trace: version() calls getPackages(cwd), which reads the workspace package.json files, before recoverInterruptedRun runs, and then re-reads them. This conflicts with 'before it reads anything else'. No test checks the order or recovery when a pre-recovery read would fail or see a half-written package.json.

A hand-written journal is placed, then package.json is set to 1.1.0, the changelog is added and the changeset removed. After version() the test asserts the 'interrupted' warning, the journal is gone and the changeset is consumed. Only the package.json/CHANGELOG/changeset-deletion state is covered; the pre-mode state (renamed changesets, pre.json, created pre dir) is not.
Asserts version 1.1.0 (not 1.2.0), exactly one '## 1.1.0' changelog heading and the changeset absent.

boundaries.boundary: journal recovery happens before any other read (getPackages, config, changesets)
interrupted state includes a half-written/invalid package.json, a moved changeset in .changeset/pre, a removed pre.json
package.json, new CHANGELOG, deleted changeset restored then versioned once

gap.missing: Recovery is not the first read: getPackages(cwd) runs first, and no test proves the order. Pre-release state (changeset moved into .changeset/pre, pre.json, created pre directory) and a corrupt journal are also not covered.
gap.reproduction: Leave a journal plus a package.json overwritten with invalid JSON (as after a kill mid-write) and run version({cwd}); it must restore, warn 'interrupted' and version normally instead of throwing from getPackages. Also spy on fs reads or getPackages to assert the journal check is first. Add a pre-mode interrupted case (changeset renamed into .changeset/pre, pre.json removed, journal preDirExisted false) and assert the exact pre-run tree is restored and the final result equals an uninterrupted run. Move recoverInterruptedRun before getPackages.
